title: Milnrow and Middleton men among 16 charged with violent disorder before Manchester football match
excerpt: Sixteen men, including defendants from Milnrow and Middleton, have been charged with violent disorder over an incident before a football match in Manchester in September 2024.
image_alt: Police file photo. Not a photograph of this event.
legal_disclaimer: This article was compiled from identified public sources and may be updated when further verified information becomes available.
right_to_reply: Anyone directly affected may request a correction or right of reply by emailing news@rochdaledaily.co.uk.

corrections.note: Corrected on 12 November 2026: an earlier version said the incident happened in Milnrow. It happened before a football match in Manchester; Milnrow is where one of the defendants lives. The earlier version also attributed statements to Greater Manchester Police that police did not make. Those passages have been removed.

body:
A Milnrow man and a Middleton man are among 16 men charged with violent disorder following an incident before a football match in Manchester.

Greater Manchester Police said the charges relate to an incident on 24 September 2024.

Those charged from the Rochdale borough are Mark Massey, of Hardman Street, Milnrow, and Ryan O'Keefe, of Thirlmere Drive, Middleton.

The other men charged are Karl Anderson, of Woodward Street, Manchester; Stefan Bezzina, of Talbot Road, Hyde; George Boylin, of Brattice Drive, Swinton; Anthony Brown, of Overdale, Bonville Road, Altrincham; John Catterall, of Meadowside Avenue, Irlam; Conor Cornforth, of Ashton Old Road, Beswick, Manchester; Jay Cornforth, of Mayton Street, Openshaw, Manchester; Harry Ellison, of Samouth Close, Miles Platting, Manchester; Jon Goulden, of Windsor Road, Newton Heath, Manchester; Robert Kompus, of Eva Street, Leigh; Dino McLeod, of Poolfield Close, Radcliffe; Callum Santos, of Thornton Avenue, Audenshaw; Ethan Thorndyke, of Sheringham Drive, Swinton; and Steven Wark, of Mossley Road, Ashton-under-Lyne.

All 16 are on bail and are due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court on Monday 4 January 2027.
